results.explanation: At the declared read_item handler-entry boundary, the task premise supplies that current_user is the authenticated active superuser and that the existing item is owned by another user. The handler loads the item by id, returns 404 only if it is absent, and denies a different-owner read only when the caller is not a superuser. With is_superuser true, that denial condition is false despite the owner mismatch, so execution reaches the return of the item. This source-visible behavior allows the read and agrees with the accepted policy. The conclusion is limited to the stated handler-entry assumptions. The supplied crop shows a CurrentUser-typed parameter but does not prove how the upstream dependency authenticates the caller, enforces active status, or binds that principal to current_user; those deployment/upstream facts are not decisive under the declared-entry premise and are not inferred here. No repository-wide or deployment completeness claim is made.

control.statement: The strongest visible authorization control raises 403 only when the caller is not a superuser and the loaded item's owner differs from the caller.
